subject: Embeddings integration: batching, normalization & migration - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@ledgerly.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: embeddings integration, migration & next steps

Hi Sarah / Alex — thanks again for the product deep-dive this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. TL;DR: Redwood can support incremental migration, flexible vector dims, and provide batching/normalization guidance to match your search/reranker stack.

Notes from the call:
- Current setup: Ledgerly has ~45M documents; embeddings live in VectorCloud today; search layer is Postgres + FAISS for reranking.
- Primary goals: reduce query latency, lower per-embedding cost, and avoid a big rip-and-reindex at cutover.
- Key integration points we discussed: SDK auth (API keys vs short-lived tokens), routing for hybrid traffic (redirect 10% to Redwood for A/B), structured output / tool-calling for downstream metadata enrichment, and embeddings/reranker parity.

Technical follow-ups (what Redwood will confirm):
1) Vector dimensions: recommend baseline options 1536 (for semantic parity with open models) and 384 for lower-cost, high-throughput use cases. We'll validate against your current VectorCloud dim (you mentioned ~768?) and run small evals.
2) Batching: suggest batching window of 5-20ms for online inference; for bulk backfill use large batch sizes (up to 1024 depending on GPU and quantization). We'll provide example batching configs.
3) Normalization: L2-normalize embeddings before indexing/search to keep cosine similarity consistent with existing FAISS workflows.
4) Migration approach: incremental backfill + aliasing strategy — shadow index on Redwood, compare QA/relevance, then cut traffic gradually. For large datasets, recommend parallelized import with checkpointing.

Attachments: I attached a migration plan and an example batching config for your infra team to review.

Next steps (proposed):
- Dev/Infra sync (technical deep dive) — schedule Wed or Thu next week (Dev to own).
- Redwood to run a 1k document eval (compute recall/MRR) using both 1536 and 384 dims.
- Provide a sample client auth snippet and routing config for your A/B plan.

If that looks right, I can get Dev to start the eval and schedule the technical session.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: embeddings integration, migration & next steps

Hey Sarah / Alex — quick technical follow-up from my side. Short answers + config pointers below. Happy to expand in the technical session.

1) Vector dims:
- If VectorCloud is currently 768, we can replicate with 768 for parity. However, for standard OpenAI-like and many open models, 1536 is common (high accuracy) and 384/512 are good low-cost options. Recommendation: run eval at 768 and 1536 if you can spare compute — should surface which dimension gives better MRR for your queries.

2) Batching & throughput:
- Online: aim for micro-batches of 8-32 tokens / requests depending on latency SLO. Use Redwood SDK's auto-batching (default window 10ms) and set max_batch_size per model.
- Bulk backfill: use our ingestion client with parallel workers; set batch_size to 512-1024 documents per GPU chunk. We included an example YAML config in example_batching_config.yaml.

3) Normalization & indexing:
- Normalize embeddings with L2 before upload. FAISS + inner product after L2 is equivalent to cosine. If you currently store raw vectors, recommend re-normalizing during migration.

4) Migration strategy (recommended):
- Phase 1: Shadow index — start copying new embeddings to Redwood in parallel while traffic still hits VectorCloud.
- Phase 2: A/B routing — 5% traffic to Redwood with evaluation hooks (we can record MRR/CTR).
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp and cutover once metrics are stable.

Misc notes:
- Auth: SDK supports long-lived API keys and short-lived JWT (recommended for client apps). We can provide example code for your security team.
- Reranker: Redwood can host both base embeddings and reranker logits; if you plan to use structured output/tool-calling, we recommend returning structured metadata alongside embeddings to avoid extra calls.

Attaching the batching config and migration plan for your infra folks.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: embeddings integration, migration & next steps

Thanks Marissa / Dev — this is very helpful. A few responses and constraints from our side:
- Confirmed: VectorCloud currently uses 768 dim vectors. Ideal outcome is parity or better for relevance.
- Constraint: our existing index store limits per-vector size to ~1024 dims today due to Postgres storage. If 1536 proves materially better we can explore storing compressed vectors but prefer to start with <=1024.
- Migration ask: we need a plan that avoids reindexing everything at once; the shadow + A/B approach sounds good. For the backfill, we have a cluster that can run parallel workers but would need the ingestion client to checkpoint every 50k docs.
- Evaluation: can you run the 1k eval against our test queries? I can send the query set and judgement file via Drive link.

Questions:
1) If we choose 768 -> do you expect any degradation vs 1536 for our corpus?
2) Can Redwood's SDK sign requests with short-lived tokens (we manage user-level auth)?

Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive — Wed 4/8 10am PT works for us.

—Sarah
